body:
PR #534 replaced the guard's orphaned-sentinel heal ("no linked worktree survives → fail open") with a per-sentinel three-state decision (fresh / live / orphaned, #472/#529). The published page https://derio-net.github.io/super-fr (docs/explainers/fr-isolation.html) still describes the old heal. The page has no committed .md source (explainers-currency known gap 1) and the rule forbids hand-editing the rendered .html, so it can't be fixed from this repo. Owed: bring the source in-repo, or re-render the affected paragraph from wherever it lives.

Side note: the plan journal has no state for a finding that is valid but deferred (only fixed | refuted), so the originating finding in 2026-09-21-sentinel-three-states was closed as 'refuted', which misdescribes it. See the correction entry in that journal.
title: Explainer fr-isolation.html describes the retired count-based self-heal (no committed source to regenerate it)

body: Split from #432 (its guard-message half shipped separately). `down --all` acts on every workspace in the repo; only workspaces with an OPEN PR are shielded, so a sibling session's pre-PR workspace (uncommitted work included) is torn down with no listing or confirmation. Wanted: print torn-down vs kept before acting, confirm when it would remove a workspace this session did not create, and extend the shield to pre-PR / dirty / unpushed workspaces. Optionally a narrower verb that clears only this session's sentinel.
title: fr isolation down --all: list blast radius and shield pre-PR/dirty workspaces (split from #432)

body:
## Summary

Acceptance-matrix evidence refs carry line anchors (`super-fr:tests/unit/test_x.py#L542`). `fr acceptance check` verifies that the referenced **file** exists; nothing verifies that the **line** still lands on the test it was recorded for. Anchors rot whenever lines are added above them, silently, and the three committed reports then link readers to the wrong place — usually the middle of an unrelated test.

## It happened twice in one day, the second time to the author of the first finding

Both on 2026-09-21, both found by eye:

1. `run-unit-review-evidence` anchored `tests/integration/test_fr_goal_shape.py#L529`; the test had been at L542 since a format fix moved it. CI was green throughout. (Journal finding `f-stale-matrix-line-anchor`, #508 review.)
2. In #527 I added four rows, then applied review fixes that inserted lines into the same test files. Three of the eight anchors I had recorded *that afternoon* no longer pointed at a `def` — one landed on an `assert` in a different test. I only noticed because I happened to print the target lines while resolving an unrelated merge conflict.

The second is the instructive one: the person who had *just written a finding about this exact defect* reproduced it within hours. It is not a discipline problem.

## How widespread, measured

Scanned `main` at the time of filing: **58** `#L` anchors into `tests/**/*.py`; **57** land on a `def test_…`/`class Test…` line; **1** does not (`run-review-findings-gate` → `test_fr_goal_shape.py#L613`, a comment I anchored deliberately inside a long test — which is its own small argument that a line is the wrong unit).

So rot is *currently repaired*, not currently widespread — by hand, by luck. And that scan has a blind spot worth stating: it cannot see an anchor that slid onto a **different** test's `def`, which looks perfectly healthy.

## Mechanism

`fr.acceptance` treats a ref as `<repo>:<path>[#L<n>]` and resolves the path. The `#L<n>` fragment is carried through to the link renderers and never interpreted. A number is the most fragile possible pointer to a test: the thing it names (a function) has a stable identity, and the ref records its least stable property.

## Shape of a fix (not a recommendation)

Ordered by how much of the problem each removes:

- **Anchor on the name, render the line.** Record `path::test_name` (pytest's own node-id spelling), and let the report renderer resolve the current line at render time. The ref then cannot rot, and `fr acceptance check` can fail at authoring on a name that does not exist — a real check, where today there is none. Existing `#L` refs migrate mechanically wherever the line currently lands on a `def` (57 of 58 today).
- **Or a tripwire**, cheaper and weaker: every `#L<n>` into a test file must land on a `def test_`/`class Test` line. Catches rot the next time CI runs; does not prevent it, and shares the blind spot above.

The first moves the failure to authoring and makes the wrong state unrepresentable; the second only reports it sooner.

## Related

- **#522** — no verb can edit a row's `acceptance` text. Same family: the matrix records things it has no way to keep true. (Disclosure: #527 hand-edited two rows' acceptance text for exactly that reason, then regenerated the reports.)
- **#508 / #527** — where the instances above were found and repaired by hand.
- `.claude/rules/acceptance-matrix.md` — describes refs; says nothing about anchors.
title: Acceptance-matrix line anchors rot silently: `#L<n>` is never checked against the test it was recorded for

body:
## Summary

On OpenCode, the agent holding a dispatched unit cannot be named **while it holds it**. The task tool blocks and returns the child session id only with the result, so `fr run claim --agent <id>` can only happen after the phase is over. During the phase, `fr run status` reads:

```
HELD BY an unclaimed agent (opencode, <model>) since …
```

#527 made fr *say* this truthfully (parity row `dispatch-holder-identity`: `opencode: partial`; the fr-goal skill now says a blocking dispatch is claimed on return). It did not close the gap. This issue is the gap.

Evidence: `docs/acceptance/evidence/2026-09-21-pr508-live-test-plan.md`, caveat C1 — the orchestrator reported learning the id "only when the task tool returned", and the status above was captured from *inside* the child, because the orchestrator could not look.

## Why it matters

#503's whole point was answering "who is holding phase 2 **right now**" — the question you have when a phase has run for an hour and you cannot tell whether its agent is alive. On OpenCode the answer today is *harness and model, never which agent*. What still works, and must keep working: the open record refuses a second dispatch whether or not anyone claimed it.

## The opening

`packages/fr-opencode-plugin` already has both halves:

- it sees a `sessionID` on every `tool.execute.before` call, the child's included;
- `src/idle.ts` already tells a child session from a top-level one (`isTopLevel`).

So on a **child** session's first tool call, the plugin knows the id the orchestrator will not learn until the end, at exactly the moment it becomes useful.

## What it would take

1. **A CLI affordance to claim without naming the unit.** The plugin knows a session id, not a step or item. Something like `fr run claim <run> --open-unit --agent <id>`: claim *the one* open, unclaimed attempt; refuse (exit 2, naming them) when there are zero or several. Phase executors run serially in one workspace, so "the one" is well defined — and the refusal is what keeps it honest when it is not.
2. **The plugin hook**: child session + first tool call + an fr run on this branch → call it once. Fail-open, silent, once per session — the same posture as the idle adapter.
3. **Finding the run** from the plugin's cwd: `fr run check --idle --format json` already resolves a run from a workspace; reuse that, do not re-derive it.

## Why this is an issue rather than a PR

It cannot be live-verified from a Claude Code session, and the repo's standard (gh#494) is that a plugin behaviour is not `enforced` until a real OpenCode session shows it executing — a green `bun test` does not. It would ship `partial`, like `fr-run-idle-guard`'s OpenCode cell, until someone drives it.

**Also unknown:** whether Hermes has the same shape. `delegate_task`'s handle timing has never been observed; the parity cell says so rather than guessing.

## Related

- **#503 / #508** — the dispatch holder record.
- **#527** — C1: made the declaration true; the parity cell's `scope_note` points here ("A plugin-side claim on the child's first tool call would close this; not built").
- **#522** — the matrix cannot express "owed a live run on harness H", which is what this would be on landing.
title: On OpenCode the holder of a dispatched unit is unnameable while it holds it — the plugin sees the child's session id first and could claim for it

body:
## Summary

`fr-isolation-guard.sh`'s orphan self-heal (#341 Task 2A) cannot tell a sentinel that has **outlived** its worktrees from one that **has not created one yet**. In a repo with no linked worktree, the first base-clone command of a brand-new pipeline — any command, `ls` included — deletes that pipeline's sentinel and exits 0. The bash guard is then inert for the rest of the session, and nothing says so.

This is the mirror image of #472 (the heal *fails* to fire when other sessions have worktrees). Same predicate, opposite failure — and **it constrains #472's fix**, see below.

Found while root-causing C4 in #527 (`docs/superpowers/journals/debug/2026-09-21-508-live-test-plan-defects.md`, entry `c4-root-cause`). It is *why* C4 hid: my first repro of "the guard denies `fr run start`" came back all-allow, because the heal had quietly removed the sentinel first.

## Repro

Using the hook's own test harness (`tests/unit/test_hooks_guard.py`: `write_sentinel`, `payload`, `run_hook`, `decision`):

1. `git init` a repo — **no** linked worktrees. Write a sentinel for session `s` with that `repo_root` (what `fr-pipeline-sentinel.sh` does when a pipeline skill loads).
2. Run the guard for **any** command with `cwd` in the repo.

Observed: `allow`, and `sentinels/s.json` is gone. Every later command in that session is ungated.

3. Add one linked worktree on any branch (anyone's) and repeat with a fresh sentinel: `deny`, sentinel kept — the intended behaviour.

So whether a new pipeline is guarded depends on whether the repo *happens* to already have someone's worktree.

## Mechanism

`hooks/fr-isolation-guard.sh`, the self-heal block:

```bash
if wt=$(git -C "$rroot" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null); then
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$wt" | grep -c '^worktree ' || true)
  if [ "${n:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
    rm -f "$sentinel" || true
    exit 0
  fi
fi
```

"Exactly one `worktree` line" is read as *the sentinel outlived all worktrees*. At pipeline start it is equally true, for the opposite reason: the pipeline's first action (`fr run start` / `fr isolation up`) has not run yet.

Ordering makes it worse. The sentinel is written when the skill **loads**; the workspace is created by the skill's first **command**. Anything the agent runs in between — and agents do run a `git status` or an `ls` first, despite the skill saying not to — takes the heal path.

## Why this matters more than it looks

It fails **open**, silently, on exactly the sessions the guard exists for: a first pipeline in a repo. Once `fr run start` has created the worktree, the repo has two `worktree` lines and the guard *would* work — but the sentinel is already gone, so it never gets the chance.

## Constraint on #472

#472's suggested fix 1 is: *"Fail open and clear the sentinel when **this session** has no live workspace, rather than when the repo has none."* A freshly started pipeline is precisely a session with no live workspace. Implemented as written, that turns this defect from "only in worktree-less repos" into "every repo, every pipeline". Whatever replaces the repo-wide count has to distinguish **never had one** from **had one, lost it**.

## Shape of a fix (not a recommendation)

Make "has this pipeline ever had a workspace" a recorded fact rather than an inference:

- stamp the sentinel when a workspace is first bound to it (`fr isolation up` / `fr run start` already know the session), and heal only a sentinel that carries the stamp and whose workspace is gone; or
- give a fresh sentinel a grace window before it is eligible for healing — cheaper, but it is a timeout standing in for a fact.

The first fails at the right place: a sentinel with no stamp is *new*, a sentinel with a stamp and no workspace is *orphaned*, and neither is guessed from `git worktree list`.

## Related

- **#472 (open)** — same predicate, opposite failure; see the constraint above.
- **#432 (open)** — what the denial says once the worktree is gone.
- **#341 / #344 / #329** — shipped the heal this is about.
- **#527** — C4, where this was found; `TestRunStartEntersIsolation` there deliberately uses a non-git dir (the heal fails closed) so its assertions are about the allowlist alone.
title: The guard's orphan self-heal retires a FRESH pipeline's sentinel: in a repo with no linked worktree, the first base-clone command disarms the guard for the whole session

body:
## Symptom

`fr plan edit <plan-dir> --step <id> --state done` re-serialises the whole phase YAML
instead of updating the one field it changes. A commit recording **nine** step ticks in a
v2 phase file showed:

```
$ git diff --numstat <base>..<head> -- docs/superpowers/plans/<slug>/02.yaml
66      80      docs/superpowers/plans/<slug>/02.yaml
```

146 changed lines to record nine one-character state flips. Every step's `text` field was
rewritten from one YAML scalar style to another:

```diff
-    text: "RED. In `<path>`, add tests that\n`load_config` on a minimal\
-      \ file yields:\n\n  - `exclude_repos == []`\n ...
+    text: |
+      RED. In `<path>`, add tests that
+      `load_config` on a minimal file yields:
```

Content identical; only the serialisation differs.

## Honest confound, so you can reproduce the right thing

In this instance the *magnitude* was amplified by me: I had earlier appended a task to
that phase with a hand-rolled `yaml.safe_dump(...)`, which wrote the double-quoted
escaped style. `fr plan edit` then normalised everything to literal block scalars on its
next write. So the diff above is "style normalisation of a hand-edited file", not purely
`fr plan edit`'s own churn.

The underlying behaviour is still worth addressing, and is independent of the confound:
**`fr plan edit` rewrites the entire file** rather than performing a surgical update. On a
file it wrote itself the styles already agree, so the diff is small — but any hand-edit,
any change to the dumper's defaults, or any future style shift converts a tick into a
whole-file rewrite.

## Why it matters

- A plan file is a review artifact. `fr-goal` puts spec, plan and journal on the branch
  precisely so a reviewer can read the plan's evolution in the PR. A 146-line diff for
  nine ticks makes the plan's real changes unreviewable — a genuine edit to a step's text
  hides in the noise.
- It defeats `git blame` on step text.
- It makes concurrent phase work more conflict-prone, which is the stated reason v2 splits
  phases into per-file YAML in the first place ("per-phase files prevent merge conflicts
  when parallel branches tick different phases"). Whole-file rewrites partially undo that
  benefit within a single phase file.

## Expected

A tick should be a one-line (or few-line) diff. Options:

1. Surgical update — parse, modify only the `state.steps.<id>` mapping, and write back
   preserving the rest byte-for-byte (e.g. `ruamel.yaml` round-trip mode, which preserves
   scalar style and comments).
2. If a full rewrite is kept, at least pin the dump style explicitly (`default_style`,
   `default_flow_style`, `width`) and normalise ONCE at `fr plan create`, so files written
   by `create` and by `edit` are byte-stable against each other.

(1) also fixes the related annoyance that any comment a human adds to a phase YAML is
silently destroyed on the next tick.

## Version

`fr 4.5.2`, v2 plan folders, `fr-goal@1`.
title: fr plan edit re-serialises the whole phase YAML to record one step tick, making plan diffs unreviewable

body:
Found during the #494 run (PR #495), journal finding `r-p1-f5` (recorded `refuted` there —
real, but out of that PR's scope; see #491 for why that label is the wrong one).

## The observation

PR #495 mirrors `plugins/super-fr/agents/fr-phase-executor.md` into
`.opencode/agent/fr-phase-executor.md`, translating the frontmatter and carrying the **body
verbatim**. The body opens with:

> Dispatch it WITHOUT `isolation: "worktree"` — fr's worktree already IS this agent's
> working copy […]
>
> If you were dispatched **with** `isolation: "worktree"`, you are in the wrong place […]
> STOP and say so — the orchestrator must re-dispatch without the flag. (A shipped hook,
> `fr-phase-executor-guard.sh`, now refuses that dispatch, so this should be unreachable;
> super-fr#420.)

`isolation: "worktree"` is a **Claude Code dispatch argument**. OpenCode has no such
argument — which is exactly why `fr-phase-executor-guard.sh` is Claude-only and why #494
scoped it out ("OpenCode has no isolation argument to refuse"). So the shipped OpenCode
agent devotes two paragraphs to telling its reader how to react to a flag that cannot exist
on their harness, and names a hook that will never fire for them.

Harmless today. But it is the **same defect class as #436's class B**, which
`fr.harness.prose.scan_prose` and `test_tripwire_skill_tool_neutrality.py` exist to close
for skills: prose naming a harness-specific mechanism as *the* way something works, copied
byte-for-byte into every harness's mirror.

## Why PR #495 did not fix it

Two reasons, both worth keeping:

- **Body byte-identity is the design** (spec §3.B), and PR #495's tests assert it. Forking
  the prose per harness at sync time is precisely what that spec's §3.C rejected for skills,
  because it turns one source into three that can disagree.
- **Agent files are not scanned.** `test_tripwire_skill_tool_neutrality.py` covers
  `plugins/super-fr/skills/*/SKILL.md` plus the two mirrors. `plugins/super-fr/agents/` is
  outside its `_SKILL_TREES`, so nothing would have caught this even if the tripwire's
  vocabulary had the right entry.

## What closing it looks like

1. **Rewrite the paragraph as a scoped clause in the canonical agent**, in the
   `**Harness — <topic>:**` shape `fr.harness.prose` already requires of skills — naming
   Claude Code (the flag, the guard hook), and stating plainly that OpenCode and Hermes have
   no isolation argument on their dispatch primitive, so there is nothing to refuse and the
   instruction does not apply. One source, correct for every reader, still byte-identical
   into the mirror.
2. **Extend the neutrality tripwire to the agents trees** — canonical
   `plugins/super-fr/agents/*.md` and the generated `.opencode/agent/*.md` — so the
   convention actually holds there. Note the mirror multiplies: after #494 one canonical
   agent generates four files, so a violation reports five times; the tripwire may want to
   report canonical-only and let the sync tripwire cover the rest.

## Decision needed first

`isolation` is a *tool argument*, not a tool name, so it does not belong in
`TOOL_VOCABULARY` as-is. Either the vocabulary grows a notion of harness-specific
*arguments*, or this particular case is handled by the clause rewrite alone (1) and the
tripwire extension (2) only guards against future tool-name leaks into agent bodies. (1)
alone is worth doing regardless and is cheap.

Related: #410 (the "adding a new harness" playbook) and #411 (extract the shared
harness_sync helper) — both are about the same seam, and this is a third instance of
"the convention exists for skills and stops at the tree boundary".
title: The canonical fr-phase-executor body names a Claude-Code-only dispatch flag, and rides verbatim into every harness mirror — agent files are outside the neutrality tripwire

body:
> **Long-lived tracking issue.** The Claude Code part can ship now. The other harnesses wait on upstream, so expect this issue to stay open until they catch up, with each harness checked off as it becomes wireable.

## Why

4.4.0 ships a status line (`plugins/super-fr/scripts/fr-statusline-claude.sh` plus the harness-neutral `fr-statusline-segment.sh`). The code works, but no harness uses it until the operator wires it up by hand, and `install.sh` never mentions it. To wire it on one host I had to:

1. read the script header and spec §5.B to find the intended path,
2. link `~/.claude/statusline.sh` → `~/.claude/plugins/cache/derio-net--super-fr/super-fr/current/scripts/fr-statusline-claude.sh` (the `current` symlink, so the link still works after an upgrade; a `…/4.4.0/…` target would stay on 4.4.0),
3. add `statusLine` to `~/.claude/settings.json`, which had no such key, so the link alone did nothing.

The spec's operator decision d1 said "ship a version for every supported harness". The installer is where that promise should reach the operator.

## Can the script be used by the other harnesses today? No, and the blockers are upstream

(Spec `2026-09-14-statusline-session-branch-design.md` §2.3 and §5.C–D, plus Codex, which the spec does not cover. Upstream status checked 2026-09-16.)

| Harness | Consumer for a command-driven status line | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `statusLine.command` in settings | ✅ works now with `fr-statusline-claude.sh` |
| Hermes Agent | `display.status_bar.custom_command` | ⛔ not shipped: NousResearch/hermes-agent#109596 is still **open**. Also `fr hermes install` copies only `hooks/`, not `scripts/` |
| Codex (next in the harness pipeline) | `tui.status_line` / `/statusline`, but only a **fixed list of built-in items** (`git-branch`, `current-dir`, `context-used`, …; `codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/status_line_setup.rs`). There is no custom-command item, and `raw-output` just means raw scrollback mode is on | ⛔ openai/codex#17827 "Customizable status line" (a Claude-style `command` hook) is **open**. The built-in `git-branch` can show the branch, but nothing can show the fr worktree or `no fr-isolation`. super-fr also has no Codex harness support yet (`fr models resolve --harness` lists only `claude-code \| opencode \| hermes`) |
| OpenCode | none | ⛔ no status-line hook: anomalyco/opencode#37464 is **open** (#30295 closed). The only option today is running `fr-statusline-segment.sh --format oneline --cwd <dir>` from a tmux/herdr status bar |

`fr-statusline-claude.sh` itself is Claude-only because it reads Claude's stdin JSON. The shared part is `fr-statusline-segment.sh --format oneline --cwd .`, which any future consumer can call.

## Ask

`scripts/install.sh` should find every harness installed on the host (it already checks for `~/.config/opencode` and `$HERMES_HOME`) and **offer** to wire the status line for each one, as far as that harness can use it:

- **Claude Code:** offer to set `statusLine` to the `current`-pathed `fr-statusline-claude.sh`.
  - `statusLine` is not a key super-fr owns, so follow the installer rules in AGENTS.md: write it only if it is **absent**, or if it already points at a super-fr status line (in that case bring it up to date). If the operator has their own status line, **never overwrite it**. Print the one-line change they could make instead, or how to call the segment with `--format ansi` from their own script.
  - `--uninstall` removes `statusLine` only if it still points at super-fr.
- **Hermes:** only offer once Hermes can read `custom_command`, detected from the Hermes version or feature, not assumed. Spec d5 is explicit that `fr hermes install` must not write a key Hermes does not read. When it becomes available, `fr hermes install` also has to copy `scripts/`. Until then, print "pending NousResearch/hermes-agent#109596".
- **Codex:** once super-fr supports Codex **and** openai/codex#17827 (or an equivalent command item) has shipped, offer to add the segment to `~/.codex/config.toml`, with the same no-clobber rule for an existing `tui.status_line`. Until then, print "pending openai/codex#17827". Optionally suggest the built-in `git-branch` item as a partial stand-in, and say clearly that it cannot show the fr-isolation state. The Codex harness work should add status-line wiring to its own checklist, so the installer doesn't have to catch up afterwards.
- **OpenCode:** print that there is no hook yet, give the tmux/herdr command, and link #37464. Offer wiring once a hook exists.

Behaviour:

- **Interactive:** one yes/no prompt per harness, with the exact change shown before anything is written.
- **Non-interactive** (`curl | bash`, CI, agent shells): **never prompt and never write** a harness's user config. Print a per-harness summary with the command to wire it by hand. (Same "no surprise writes when nothing is watching" principle as the artifact-migration gate.)
- Running the installer again changes nothing once the status line is wired.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fresh host with Claude Code and no `statusLine`: interactive yes → `statusLine` is set; the next session shows branch and worktree lines
- [ ] Existing custom `statusLine`: left untouched, and hand-wiring instructions are printed
- [ ] Non-interactive install: no harness config file changes (mtime and content unchanged)
- [ ] `--uninstall` removes only a super-fr-owned `statusLine`
- [ ] Claude Code: shippable now
- [ ] Hermes: wired once hermes-agent#109596 ships (and `fr hermes install` copies `scripts/`)
- [ ] Codex: wired once super-fr supports Codex and openai/codex#17827 ships
- [ ] OpenCode: wired once anomalyco/opencode#37464 ships
- [ ] Until each ships: a clear "pending upstream" message with the link, and nothing is written
- [ ] Tests in the `tests/unit/test_install_sh.py` style; acceptance-matrix row; version bump (touches `install.sh`)
title: install.sh: offer to wire the fr status line into each installed harness (Claude Code, Hermes, Codex, OpenCode)

body:
## Summary

The #341 Task 2 fix for the orphaned-sentinel deadlock (#329, shipped in #344) only works in a repo with a **single** active session.

- **Sentinels are per-session.** The file is `~/.cache/fr/sentinels/<session_id>.json`.
- **Everything that removes them is repo-scoped.** That covers the guard's self-heal, the eager clear in `fr isolation down`, and `clear_repo_sentinels()`.
- **The gc reap never touches them.**

So a session whose own workspace gets gc-reaped after its PR merges stays **locked out of every base-clone command** for as long as any other session has a worktree in that repo. The inverse also holds: when the repo-wide clear does fire, it drops **other live sessions'** sentinels too.

Observed on fr **4.3.0** / super-fr **4.3.0**, `derio-net/frank`, 2026-09-14, during an fr-goal close-out. Four fr workspaces from different sessions were live at the time.

## Repro (observed live)

1. An fr-goal run holds session sentinel `d6663735-….json` (`repo_root: …/frank`). Its workspace is `chore/paperclip-doc-touchups`.
2. Its PR (#382) merges. gc reaps the workspace:
   ```
   gc: chore/paperclip-doc-touchups: merged → reaped
   ```
   (`~/.cache/fr/isolation-gc.log`; the log never mentions a sentinel.)
3. The session sentinel survives, and `fr isolation status` no longer lists the branch.
4. Every Bash command from the session is denied with the standard "fr pipeline active — ALL base-repo commands are gated" message, including a bare `cd <old worktree> && pwd`. The old worktree dir is gone; that part is #432.
5. **The #341 self-heal does not fire**, because `git -C <repo> worktree list --porcelain` reports **6** `worktree` lines, not 1:
   ```
   worktree ~/Docs/projects/DERIO_NET/frank
   worktree ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/docs__paperclip-382-closeout
   worktree ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/feat__staging-vcluster-gate     # another session
   worktree ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/fix__etcd-scrape-vmstaticscrape # another session
   worktree ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/fix__ovms-rerank-oom-guard      # another session
   worktree ~/Docs/projects/DERIO_NET/frank/.claude/worktrees/agent-…   # a Claude subagent worktree
   ```
6. The only escape was the one #329 already described: `FR_ISOLATION_TARGET=worktree fr isolation up --branch <new-branch>`, which creates a fresh workspace just to make the `cd` escape satisfiable again. I needed a close-out branch anyway, so that was acceptable here. A session with nothing further to do in the repo would be creating a workspace purely to regain `git status`.

## Mechanism: three scoping mismatches

### 1. The guard self-heal counts worktrees repo-wide

`hooks/fr-isolation-guard.sh`, lines ~272-286:

```bash
if wt=$(git -C "$rroot" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null); then
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$wt" | grep -c '^worktree ' || true)
  if [ "${n:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
    rm -f "$sentinel" || true
    exit 0
  fi
fi
```

"Zero linked worktrees in the repo" stands in for "this pipeline's workspace is gone". The two are equivalent only with one session. Any other session's workspace keeps `n > 1`, and so does any unrelated linked worktree: a Claude `isolation: "worktree"` subagent checkout, or a hand-made `.worktrees/` checkout. When that happens the orphaned sentinel is never healed.

### 2. `fr isolation down` clears sentinels only when the whole repo has zero workspaces

`fr/commands/isolation_cmd.py`, lines ~463-470:

```python
# #399: when this was the last workspace, clear the pipeline sentinel(s)
# eagerly. ... scoped to "zero workspaces remain".
if not list_states(root):
    clear_repo_sentinels(root)
```

This is the same proxy as the guard. A session tearing down its **own** last workspace keeps its sentinel whenever another session has one.

### 3. `clear_repo_sentinels()` over-clears: every session's sentinel for the repo

`fr/isolation/types.py`, `clear_repo_sentinels(repo_root)`, removes **every** sentinel whose `repo_root` matches, whatever session wrote it:

```python
if root and str(Path(root).resolve()) == target:
    f.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```

So when the repo-wide condition is met, or on `fr isolation down --all`, other **live** sessions lose their sentinels. Their guard disarms silently, and the base-clone write protection the guard exists for is gone mid-pipeline. This is the mirror image of mismatch 2.

### 4. Nothing collects orphaned sentinels

The gc reap (`fr/isolation/local.py`, the `GcAction … "reaped"` path) removes the worktree and never looks at sentinels. Sentinels of ended sessions therefore accumulate, as #329's second comment already noted. At the time of this report `~/.cache/fr/sentinels/` held:

| sentinel | repo | started | session binding (`~/.cache/fr/sessions/`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `d6663735…` | frank | 2026-09-13T19:30:51Z | none (this session; its workspace was reaped) |
| `3e172cfa…` | frank | 2026-09-13T19:30:36Z | none |
| `557328da…` | frank | 2026-09-13T13:24:27Z | none |
| `06697a53…` | herdr-setup | 2026-09-13T19:45:12Z | bound |

## Suggested fix

Scope every sentinel operation to the **session and its workspaces**, not the repo:

1. **Guard self-heal.** Fail open and clear the sentinel when **this session** has no live workspace, rather than when the repo has none. Session bindings already exist (#449, `~/.cache/fr/sessions/<session-id>.json`, plus the workspace state). Possible checks:
   - no workspace state bound to `session_id` whose worktree dir still exists; or
   - if bindings are absent (as here: the run began with `fr run start`, which never attached), no valid `.fr-isolation` marker in any fr worktree for this repo that the session has touched.

   Either way, a repo-wide `git worktree list` count is the wrong signal.
2. **`fr isolation down` eager clear.** Clear the **caller's** sentinel when the caller has no remaining workspaces. Do not wait for the repo to have none.
3. **`clear_repo_sentinels()`.** Take a session id, or at least exclude sentinels whose session still has a live bound workspace. Otherwise `down --all` should say that it disarms the guard for N other sessions.
4. **gc reap.** When reaping a workspace, clear the sentinels of sessions bound to it that have no other live workspace. Also age out sentinels with no session binding and no live workspace, rather than keeping them forever.

## Related

- **#432 (open).** Covers the deny message when the `cd` target is gone, and the unconditional `down --all` advertisement. Different root; this issue explains why the lockout "never lifts on its own".
  - One data point for #432: on 4.3.0, `fr isolation verify-merge --branch <reaped-branch>` **does** work after the reap. It reported `✓ changes present on origin/main, PR MERGED` for the reaped branch, so that half of #432 looks fixed.
- **#341 / #344.** Shipped the self-heal and `down --all` whose scoping this report is about.
- **#329.** The original orphaned-sentinel deadlock report, whose repro was a single-session close-out.
- **#399.** Introduced the "zero workspaces remain" eager clear in `down`.
- **#449.** Session bindings, the natural key for session-scoped clearing.
title: Sentinel self-heal and clearing are repo-scoped: a reaped workspace locks its session out whenever other sessions have worktrees (#341 fix only holds single-session)

body:
## Problem

`fr isolation` has no way to pause a workspace. The only lifecycle verbs are `up`, `restart`, and `down`, and `gc` only tears down workspaces whose PR has **merged**. A workspace with an open PR, or with no PR yet, keeps its devcontainer running until someone runs `down`, which also removes the worktree.

On a laptop with many long-lived workspaces this adds up. Observed on one host (macOS, Docker Desktop, 64 GB RAM):

- 17 isolation workspaces across several repos; 8 devcontainers running, some idle for 3+ days.
- `fr isolation gc --dry-run`: 14 `open → skipped`, 3 `no-pr → warned`. Nothing to reap.
- The containers themselves used about 300 MB in total, but the Docker Desktop VM held about 7.7 GB RSS and about 100% CPU (virtiofs and VM overhead scale with the number of running containers and bind-mounted worktrees).
- The host was swapping hard (22 GB swap used) and the CPU was throttled. Stopping idle containers was the obvious relief, but fr offers no command for it.

The workaround today is plain `docker stop <container>`. That works, but it is outside fr: the operator must map container names (`vsc-<branch>-<hash>-features`, random docker names) back to workspaces by hand, and fr does not tell them how to resume.

## What the code does today (fr 4.x, `fr/isolation/local.py`)

- `_docker_ps` uses `docker ps --all`, so `status` and `restart` already see a stopped container.
- `restart` runs `docker restart`, which also **starts** a stopped container. So `fr isolation restart --branch <b>` already works as a resume, but nothing documents this.
- `up` is idempotent on an existing worktree, and `devcontainer up` starts an existing stopped container. So `up --branch <b>` is a second resume path.
- `exec` calls `devcontainer exec` directly with no start step. Against a stopped container it fails instead of resuming or explaining the fix.

## Proposal

1. **`fr isolation stop [--branch <b>] [--all-idle]`**: `docker stop` the workspace container. Keep the worktree, the state record, and session bindings. `status` shows `container=stopped`.
2. **`exec` on a stopped container**: either start it (`docker start`, then exec) or fail with a one-line fix: "container is stopped; run `fr isolation up --branch <b>` (or `restart`)".
3. **Optional `gc --stop-idle[=<duration>]`**: for `open` and `no-pr` workspaces, stop (never remove) containers with no bound live session and no `exec` activity within the window. This keeps `gc` non-destructive for unmerged work (see #435 for why destructive gc on unmerged or dirty work is dangerous), while giving scheduled or opportunistic gc a way to release resources.
4. **Docs**: state in the `restart` and `up` help that they resume a stopped container.

## Acceptance

- `fr isolation stop --branch <b>` leaves the worktree and state intact; `status` reports the container as stopped.
- `fr isolation up --branch <b>` or `restart` brings it back with in-container installs preserved.
- `fr isolation exec` against a stopped container either resumes it or prints the resume command, and never fails with a raw devcontainer error.
- `gc --stop-idle` never stops a container whose workspace has a live bound session, and never removes a worktree.

Related: #354 (gc lifecycle), #423 (gc across modes), #435 (gc on dirty worktrees), #307 (restart).
title: fr isolation: no way to stop idle devcontainers without destroying the workspace (add `stop`, stopped-aware `exec`, opt-in `gc --stop-idle`)

body:
Two problems that compound. Hit during a long `fr-goal` run on `derio-net/frank` (fr **3.19.0**) with three unrelated sessions live in the same repo.

## 1. A reaped worktree turns the `cd` escape into a total, unexplained lockout

`fr`'s gc reconciles merged workspaces, so once a PR merges its worktree under `~/.cache/fr/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>/` is **deleted**.

Every subsequent command of the prescribed shape then fails:

```bash
cd ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/feat__blog-igpu-retrieval && git status
```

The `cd` fails (directory gone), so `fr-isolation-guard.sh` sees the session cwd still inside the base repo and denies the whole command — including a bare `ls`, `cat` or `find`. The denial is the standard message:

> fr pipeline active — ALL base-repo commands are gated (not just git/gh) … lead with `cd <worktree> && …` to work from the worktree cwd.

Which is advice the operator **is already following**. Nothing distinguishes "you forgot to cd" from "the directory you are cd-ing into no longer exists", so it reads as the guard misbehaving. It is more confusing still because the identical command worked minutes earlier, and because the pipeline stays active on *other* sessions' sentinels, so it never lifts on its own.

**Suggested fix:** when the command leads with `cd <path>` and `<path>` does not exist, say so:

> `<path>` no longer exists — an fr worktree is removed once its branch merges. Start a new workspace with `fr isolation up --branch <name>`, or `cd` into a live one (`fr isolation status`).

That one line would have saved a handful of dead-end commands.

**Related, same root:** `fr isolation verify-merge --branch <b>` fails *after* the merge it exists to verify, because the workspace is already gone:

```
error: no isolation workspace for branch 'ops/igpu-retrieval-archive'.
```

The `fr-goal` skill prescribes exactly this as step 9's first action ("**first verify it reached `main`** via `fr isolation verify-merge --branch <b>`"). If gc has already run, the tool cannot answer and the operator falls back to `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>` by hand. Worth either resolving the branch without a live workspace, or reporting "workspace already reaped; checked `origin/main` directly".

## 2. The guard advertises `down --all` unconditionally

The same message ends:

> No worktree left? `fr isolation down --all` clears the pipeline.

To an operator staring at a lockout, that is the obvious next command. But `--all` acts on **every** workspace in the repo, and a session has no visibility into how many belong to other sessions.

Correcting my own first reading, in fairness to the current design: `_down_all` is not indiscriminate.

> A workspace whose PR is still OPEN is KEPT (never silently destroyed) unless `--force` — that open-PR check is the only IsolationError `down` raises

So open-PR workspaces are protected. In my case all three concurrent workspaces had open PRs (#733, #750, #756) and would have survived.

**The gap is the pre-PR state.** A workspace that has not opened its PR yet has no shield, and plain `--all` tears it down. That is precisely the state a session occupies for most of an `fr-goal` run — mine were pre-PR for hours. So the guard's own suggestion can destroy a sibling session's in-progress workspace, including uncommitted work, with no confirmation and no listing of what it is about to remove.

### Suggestions, roughly in order of value

- **Make `--all` show its blast radius and confirm.** Print what will be torn down versus kept before acting — `2 workspaces: tearing down ops/foo (no PR); keeping feat/bar (PR #733 open)` — and require confirmation when it would remove a workspace this session did not create.
- **Extend the shield to pre-PR workspaces**, or at minimum to any workspace with a dirty tree or unpushed commits. The open-PR check protects the *least* vulnerable state and skips the most vulnerable one.
- **Stop advertising `--all` unconditionally in the guard message.** For the "no worktree left" case the right advice is nearly always `fr isolation up --branch <name>` — allowed from the base repo, since it is an `fr isolation …` command, and you usually need a branch for close-out work anyway. Reserve `--all` for the genuine orphaned-sentinel deadlock it was added for (#341), and point at `fr isolation status` first.
- Consider a narrower verb for the common case: clear only *this* session's sentinel rather than acting on every workspace in the repo.

## Environment

fr 3.19.0, macOS, `derio-net/frank`, three concurrent sessions. Guard message quoted from `hooks/fr-isolation-guard.sh:109`; `--all` semantics from `fr/commands/isolation_cmd.py::_down_all` and `fr isolation down --help`.

Possibly adjacent to #421 (cd-allowance gaps), but distinct: that one is about *other repos* being unreachable; this is about a *reaped* worktree in the same repo, plus the remedy the guard recommends for it.
title: Guard denial after a gc-reaped worktree is indistinguishable from the normal one, and it advertises 'down --all' to a session that cannot see other workspaces

limited (no `kubectl`), so PR #314 cannot be finished/verified right now. PR set
to **draft** until Omni is back.

1. Re-rebase `feat/secrets-injection` onto current `origin/main`.
2. **Resolve carefully:** version-source files (re-bump via
   `scripts/bump-version.py`, → 3.5.x) **and** the fr-isolation skill/rule docs.
   ⚠️ #328/#330 ("enforce invariants over prose: fr-isolation Edit/Write hook")
   reworked the **same** fr-isolation SKILL/rule docs this PR edits (GH_TOKEN
   boundary, `--secret` docs) — expect non-trivial conflicts beyond versions,
   and confirm #314's changes still **compose** with the new hook enforcement.
3. Run the full in-container gate (ruff/format/mypy/version-sync/pytest); the
   stale-uv-tool bridge-test failure after a version bump is fixed with
   `uv tool install --force` (not a regression).
4. Force-push (with lease), mark **Ready for review**.
5. **Phase 5 (operator-owned, needs the cluster):** create the Infisical
   read-only short-TTL Universal-Auth machine identity, export
   `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID` / `FR_INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET` on the host
   (Keychain helper available), run a real
   `fr isolation exec --secret <KEY> -- printenv <KEY>` smoke test, record with
   `fr plan edit <plan-dir> --complete-phase 5 --note "<what was verified>"`.
6. Post-merge close-out: `fr archive` the plan + housekeeping PR;
   `fr isolation down` the `feat/secrets-injection` workspace.
